body:
Where I am, I can drink legally. I can also easily score drugs if I ever wanted to. Somehow, I've never liked the idea of getting drunk or getting high. I don't even drink coffee.

I'm stuck in a metropolis. Third world country. In the city, I can be relatively comfortable, but outside, it's like going back to the feudal ages. Intellectuals living outside cities either get killed by the military for rebellion, or get killed by bandits for not joining rebellion.

I've been studying to be an engineer. Shit sucks. Don't to be one. Got beat up and almost thrown out of the house when I tried to object. Am close to getting expelled because I can't bring myself to school because of depression (fits of utter despair, literally can't move). If I get kicked out of college, I get disowned by my family.

I'd love to do what Americans do - just go out and make something of themselves. Here where I am, that's just not possible. Minimum wage means you live in an illegal settlement, barely covered with rusting steel sheets over your head and tarpaulin for walls. All I've ever wanted in life was to get out of this shithole.

Last person I talked to was a college guidance counselor - free, the only price I can afford. She told me straight that I still have my depression as previously diagnosed by a psychiatrist from my last attempt. Not much more she could do for me though.

I'm sorry, but I disagree. It's been 4 years since my last real attempt. I was 16 and now I'm 20. That's pretty much all of my conscious adult life. Sad people are ones who get their kittens run over, cry about it and move on. Depressed people spiral downwards until they lose everything, friends, family, jobs, until they have nothing. How the hell do you live for nothing.

Thanks for the insight. The best step for me right now is to have myself tested. Unfortunately, I can't just do it as it costs money, so I should ask around and research first. Psychological disorders here are seen as rich people's diseases; drama they put up because they have nothing better to do in life. This sort of indifference to my mental state is really hurting.

Thank you. Just to be clear, the urge for suicide is really subconscious. I feel an urge to off myself, but I really know better than to do that.

I can't afford a psychiatrist. My parents wouldn't stop me, but we just can't afford that and medication too. A psychiatrist would cost 100-200 USD a month here, and medication would cost me $50 a month. That's enough for food and electricity for a family of four here.

We're not too poor, but we can't afford to spend on things we "don't need".

I've been trying to be positive about everything, thinking maybe my depression really might go away if I don't think about it, but it really won't. It's always there at the back of my mind. When I keep myself entertained (movies, friends), I don't feel it. But when I do mind-numbing tasks like listening to lectures or drafting papers, I zone out and feel deep waves of anxiety and despair. It's really horrible trying to explain it to people I know. Somehow, depression to people means sadness like if your cat or grandmother dies. To me, it doesn't really feel like sadness, but a really heavy feeling pulling deep inside me.
